title: One of You, or the Finest of You?
arabic: لَقَدْ جَآءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ عَزِيزٌ عَلَيْهِ مَا عَنِتُّمْ حَرِيصٌ عَلَيْكُم بِٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ رَءُوفٌ رَّحِيمٌ
translation: “There has come to you a Messenger from your own selves - your suffering grieves him, he is anxious over you; to the believers, kind and merciful.”

shia.label: Shia emphasis
shia.body: Shia tafsir treasures a reading remembered from Fāṭima - min anfasikum, 'from the noblest of you': a purified, chosen line, answering Ibrāhīm's prayer for a Messenger raised from his own descendants.

sunni.label: Sunni emphasis
sunni.body: Sunni tafsir hears min anfusikum, 'from your own selves': a Messenger human like you - your tongue, your kin - one you already know and trust, so his mercy is lived close.

voiceover.hook: In this verse, one word about the Prophet's origin has been read two ways for over a thousand years.
voiceover.reference: Surah at-Tawbah, verse one hundred twenty-eight.
voiceover.payoff: One vowel apart. Born one of you - and born the finest of you.
voiceover.question: Which of these two readings resonates with you

caption_desc: In the week of his birth - one verse, two ways of hearing where he came from 🌙 #quran #tafsir #shia #sunni #prophetmuhammad #mawlid #islam
